items.label: section_header
items.text: 17 ACIDS, BASES AND SALT PREPARATIONS

items.label: text
items.text: Acids were introduced in Chapter 16. In this chapter we will look more closely at some of the reactions of acids and how to make salts.

items.label: section_header
items.text: LEARNING OBJECTIVES

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know the general rules for predicting the solubility of ionic compounds in water:

items.label: list_item
items.text: common sodium, potassium and ammonium compounds are soluble

items.label: list_item
items.text: all nitrates are soluble

items.label: list_item
items.text: common chlorides are soluble, except those of silver and lead(II)

items.label: list_item
items.text: common hydroxides are insoluble except for those of sodium, potassium and calcium (calcium hydroxide is slightly soluble)

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand acids and bases in terms of proton transfer

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand that an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe the reactions of hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid and nitric acid with metals, bases and metal carbonates (excluding the reactions between nitric acid and metals) to form salts

items.label: section_header
items.text: SALTS

items.label: text
items.text: All acids contain hydrogen. When that hydrogen is replaced by a metal, the compound formed is called a salt. Magnesium sulfate is a salt, and so is zinc chloride, and so is potassium nitrate.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 17.1 Sodium chloride is common salt. You don't normally make it. It occurs naturally.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that metal oxides, metal hydroxides and ammonia can act as bases, and that alkalis are bases that are soluble in water

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe an experiment to prepare a pure, dry sample of a soluble salt, starting from an insoluble reactant

items.label: list_item
items.text: Practical: Prepare a sample of pure, dry hydrated copper(Il) sulfate crystals, starting from copper(Il) oxide

items.label: section_header
items.text: CHEMISTRY ONLY

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe an experiment to prepare a pure, dry sample of a soluble salt, starting from an acid and alkali.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe an experiment to prepare a pure, dry sample of an insoluble salt, starting from two soluble reactants.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Practical: Prepare a sample of pure, dry lead(II) sulfate
